fact: La Nation states that article 576 of the Code du numerique provides five years' imprisonment and a FCFA 25 million fine for publishing online, without consent, a montage of a person's image or words whose artificial character is not evident or flagged.
Forum on Information and Democracy and ALCRER state that Benin has no specific, sufficiently binding AI regulation or liability regime for AI uses, and no specific AI regulatory authority.

Benin's national digital investigations centre (CNIN) reminded on 29 May 2026 that using AI to alter, generate or share a person's image without consent is punishable under article 576 of the Digital Code by up to five years in prison and a fine of FCFA 25 million.

Levellers says Benin's Digital Code (Loi 2017-20, promulgated 20 April 2018, amended 2021) regulates profiling and automated individual decisions (Article 401) and requires impact assessments for high-risk automated processing, the only binding rules touching AI harms.
